heading: Observational commands, one console at a time
introduction: Use an authorized console or SSH session to the named device, in the correct administrative context. Check the installed release's help before running a command. These examples observe state; they do not repair the network. Run short samples, not unattended collection on an overloaded appliance.
privacyNote: Save timestamps and sanitize addresses, device identifiers and customer data before sharing output. Do not invent output or run a command on a different product because its name looks similar.

checks.observation: Record user, system, interrupt and idle proportions, along with available workload indicators. Repeat a short sample to distinguish a transient peak from persistent load.
checks.limit: The overall figures do not identify the faulty switch or prove a forwarding loop. They select the next investigation.
checks.stop: A snapshot command returns to the prompt.

checks.observation: Sample at two-second intervals and compare the CPU categories across cores. Preserve a few timestamped samples.
checks.limit: High interrupt work can justify traffic investigation, but is not proof of a loop, attack or firmware defect.
checks.stop: Press any key to quit, as indicated by the documented command prompt.

checks.observation: Identify busy processes when application CPU needs investigation. Press p to sort by CPU in the documented FortiOS 7.6.8 view.
checks.limit: This process list is not the entire system and interrupt workload. Do not terminate a process based on its ranking.
checks.stop: Press q to return to the normal CLI prompt.

checks.observation: Compare incoming and outgoing packets per second on the relevant interfaces with baseline and unaffected paths.
checks.limit: A high rate identifies a candidate path, not a proven faulty cable. Hardware and release behavior must be considered.
checks.stop: Record the displayed result; do not script continuous polling. If your release behaves differently, consult its CLI help before continuing.

checks.observation: On the switch console, compare local ports with advertised neighboring devices and the physical cable map. Reference: FortiSwitch 7.6.2.
checks.limit: No LLDP entry is not proof of no cable. Discovery may be disabled or unsupported, and LLDP does not prevent loops.
checks.stop: The display command returns to the prompt.

checks.observation: On the switch console, inspect root, port roles and states for the relevant instance and compare adjacent switches. Reference: FortiSwitch 7.6.4.
checks.limit: One snapshot does not prove every VLAN is loop-free. A discarding redundant port can be correct protection; do not force it to forward.
checks.stop: The display command returns to the prompt.
